question: A continuous production model uses real quantities x and y. Its constraints are x >= 1/2, y >= 0, x + 2y <= 7, and 3x + y <= 8. Draw and shade the common feasible region, label every exact corner, and maximise profit F = 4x + 5y. Put F at each corner and mark every maximiser. Mark A = (1,1), B = (0,1), C = (9/5,13/5), and state feasibility. Fractional production is permitted.

qualitativeClaims.expected: The unique maximiser is C=(9/5,13/5), with maximum profit 101/5.
A=(1,1) is feasible; B=(0,1) is infeasible because 0<1/2; C=(9/5,13/5) is feasible and lies at the intersection of the two sloping boundaries.
